subject: Archaeology
title: Seriation: Dating by Style
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Seriation: Dating by Style.

hook.text: Before radiocarbon dating existed, archaeologists dated sites by tracking how pottery styles changed over time.

buildup.text: Seriation arranges artifacts by style. Designs start rare, become popular, then fade — creating a predictable arc.

discovery.text: Flinders Petrie pioneered the method in Egypt in the 1890s, ordering thousands of graves by their pottery alone.

twist.text: Seriation gives relative dates — older or newer than — but not absolute dates.

climax.text: Combined with radiocarbon, seriation becomes powerful. Style gives the sequence; science gives the year.

punchline.text: Fashion changes — even in pottery. Track the trends and you track time.

quiz.question: What does seriation provide that absolute dating does not?
options: The cultural sequence of styles and their relative order
The exact calendar year an artifact was made
The geographic origin of the raw materials used

details.summary: Seriation arranges artifacts in chronological order based on changing styles — pottery decorations, tool shapes, or building designs. Like fashion trends, artifact styles rise in popularity, peak, and decline. Tracking these patterns creates a relative timeline for sites lacking absolute dates.
details.whyItMatters: Before scientific dating, seriation was one of the only ways to establish chronological order. It remains useful when absolute dating is impossible and reveals how cultural preferences changed over time.
takeaways: Arranges artifacts chronologically by tracking style changes
Works on the principle that styles follow predictable popularity curves
Provides relative dates when absolute dating methods are unavailable

faq.question: How does seriation work in practice?
faq.answer: Archaeologists count artifact types at each site or layer. A style that appears rarely, becomes common, then disappears again follows a battleship-shaped frequency curve. Arranging assemblages so these curves align in sequence produces a relative chronological order.

faq.question: What are the limitations of seriation?
faq.answer: It provides relative order but not calendar dates. It assumes styles change gradually and uniformly, which isn't always true. Regional variations mean seriation sequences from one area may not apply to another. It works best as a complement to absolute dating methods.
